name: Duloxetine
metabolism: CYP1A2 and CYP2D6 mediate hepatic oxidation, followed by glucuronide or sulfate conjugation. Major circulating metabolites do not contribute substantially to activity; elimination is mainly urinary as metabolites.
summary: Duloxetine is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) used to treat major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, fibromyalgia, neuropathic pain, and other chronic pain conditions.
toxicities: DailyMed warnings include suicidal thoughts/behavior, potentially fatal liver injury, serotonin syndrome, bleeding, orthostatic hypotension/falls/syncope, blood-pressure increases, hyponatremia, seizures, mania/hypomania, severe skin reactions, and discontinuation symptoms.
Common adverse reactions in adults include nausea, dry mouth, somnolence, constipation, decreased appetite, and sweating.
generalRisks: The label is for oral delayed-release capsules (updated 2025-08-29). About hepatotoxicity (including hepatic failure), serotonin syndrome, bleeding, falls/syncope, increased blood pressure, hyponatremia, seizures, mania/hypomania and discontinuation symptoms. The label advises avoiding use with substantial alcohol use or chronic liver disease.
saferUse: Avoid use with substantial alcohol use or chronic liver disease as specified by the label; seek medical evaluation for jaundice or other signs of liver injury.
Monitor blood pressure during prescribed use. Seek urgent care for severe fainting, seizure, severe rash/blistering, or suspected serotonin syndrome.
Do not stop abruptly; gradually reduce under clinical guidance. Check before combining with serotonergic agents, MAOIs, CYP1A2 inhibitors, thioridazine, antiplatelet drugs, or anticoagulants.
dosageRemark: The label is a prescription oral delayed-release capsule label. Its therapeutic regimen is not recreational dose guidance; no recreational threshold or duration is established here.
